placements.why: This envelope's content — an observatory instrument's frequency calibration checked against dated reference plates — is organizationally distinct from the consulting-methodology decisions (Diagnostic First, Knowledge Mapping) that populate ns__Strategy in the existing map. Nothing in the supplied strata (currently empty) or existing structure covers instrument/measurement verification as an organizational category, and the perspective's own vocabulary names 'Calibration' as a recognized top-level stratum. Minting it foundational (no under) since it is a peer category to Strategy, not a child of it.
placements.title: instrument readiness as its own organizational category, distinct from strategy or delivery decisions
placements.frame: What has been brought into verified working order, against what standard, and is that verification still current?

placements.title: calibration moves from adjustment to settled fact once checked against an independent reference standard
placements.frame: Has this instrument's calibration been checked against a named, dated external reference, and does it hold across the full operating range it claims to cover?
placements.why: All three expressions carry the same recurring subject future calibration envelopes will keep feeding: an instrument (Kestrelwood spectrograph) whose setting (88.4 MHz) is ratified as settled by verification against a named external standard (June reference plates), holding across the full observing band. src-1 is the prose statement of this in Quill's voice; src-2 and src-3 restate the identical content as structured metadata fields on the same footing. Per the grain test, the specific numbers (88.4 MHz, June plates) are the evidence, not the leaf — the leaf is the recurring theme of calibration-verified-against-standard that this and future observatory envelopes will accumulate under. Nothing in the supplied structure (empty) or the visible map (consulting-methodology decisions under ns__Strategy) plausibly holds this theme, so no reuse candidate exists.
